deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is a small category, A^ is the presheaf topos, X is a topos, and φ: A → X is a functor. φ_!: A^ → X is its colimit-preserving (Kan) extension, φ_!(F) = colim_{A/F} φ(α). The previous page lists three conditions on representables: a) φ_!(e_{A^}) → e_X; b) φ_!(α×β) → φ(α)×φ(β); c) φ_!(α×_{α0}β) → φ(α)×_{φ(α0)}φ(β). There they are stated with 'epi'. Grothendieck remarks that they become isomorphisms when φ_! = f* for a geometric morphism f: X → A^, and conjectures the converse.

On this page he takes the iso versions (Hyp 1, 2, 2'), which concern representables, and extends them to arbitrary presheaves:
- b') φ_!(F×G) ≅ φ_!F×φ_!G for all F, G.
- c') φ_!(G×_F H) ≅ φ_!G×_{φ_!F}φ_!H for all spans in A^.
The argument, sketched on the previous page, writes F = colim_{A/F} α and uses that φ_! preserves colimits and that colimits are universal in A^ and in X.

Hence the single equivalent form (Hyp): φ_! commutes with all finite limits. He adds that it suffices to require this for diagrams of representables of the three shapes: empty (terminal object), discrete pair (product) and cospan (fibre product). He ends by asking whether Hyp can hold without φ_! being exact, and when.

Purpose: this is a criterion for a functor from a site-like category A into a topos X to be (the inverse image of) a geometric morphism X → A^. It is the flatness / 'filtering functor' criterion, a preliminary in the notes on stratified topoi.
errors: As literally stated, the closing question is vacuous. φ_! is always right exact, since it preserves colimits. Hyp (iso version) says exactly that φ_! preserves finite limits. So Hyp is equivalent to exactness of φ_!, i.e. to φ_! = f* for a geometric morphism. The non-trivial question is presumably about the EPI versions a), b), c) of the previous page; 'cette hypothèse' probably refers back to those.

Possible gap: from b) and the colimit decomposition one gets b') for all presheaves. For c') the colimit argument reduces only to fibre products α×_F β of representables over an ARBITRARY presheaf F, not over a representable α0. Equalizers (e.g. the pullback along a diagonal α → α×α) are not obviously reached from fibre products over representables when A lacks finite limits. The standard flatness criteria use equalizers explicitly. The claim 'il suffit de le postuler quand les F_i sont dans A, et dans les trois cas particuliers' is clear when A has finite limits, but is not justified on the page in general. (A small check with A the parallel-pair category produced no counterexample.)

In the epi form, the conditions of the previous page are (up to the equalizer issue) exactly the 'filtering functor' conditions. These are known to be equivalent to flatness, hence to exactness of φ_!. So the epi version already forces exactness, and the answer to 'quand ?' is essentially 'always', provided the equalizer condition is included.

ideas.what: Extending finite-limit preservation of φ_! from representables to all presheaves, via the canonical colimit presentation and universality of colimits in a topos
ideas.modern_name: Flat functors / Diaconescu's theorem: φ_! is left exact iff φ is flat (filtering)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Verdier (SGA 4, Exp. I and IV); Diaconescu (1975); textbook form in Mac Lane–Moerdijk VII.8–9
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. IV (morphisms of topoi into presheaf topoi, flat functors); SGA 4 Exp. I

ideas.what: Reduction of the finite-limit condition to three shapes: terminal object, binary products, fibre products over objects of A
ideas.modern_name: Finite limits generated by terminal object and pullbacks; criteria for filtering functors
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. I (finite limits), Exp. IV

ideas.what: Question whether the epi (rather than iso) comparison conditions can hold without φ_! being exact
ideas.modern_name: Filtering vs flat functors (they coincide when the target is a topos)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working-through of the standard flatness criterion for the Kan extension φ_! (SGA 4 / Diaconescu). The only notable feature is the possibly unjustified reduction to fibre products over representables, plus an open-ended question whose answer is known: filtering = flat when the target is a topos. Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The final line reads 'Mais cette hypothèse peut-elle être vérifiée, sans que φ_! soit exact : Quand ?' — the transcription is correct; 'Quand ?' is on its own line.
In c'), the right-hand side is φ_!(G)×_{φ_!(F)}φ_!(H), with the subscript φ_!(F) written under the ×; the transcription is correct.
The three diagram shapes are drawn as '•', '••' and a cospan '↘•↙'; the transcription's ↘↙ is acceptable.
